title: GPU OOM + CUDA driver mismatch scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Local repro on infra dev box (gcloud vm with A100s) while trying to run model conversion and a smoke serve of a 7B fp16 model.
- Symptoms: intermittent OOMs on both training-style scripts and inference, sometimes accompanied by CUDA runtime/driver errors after package changes.

Commands run (most relevant outputs trimmed):
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.113.01    Driver Version: 535.113.01    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM4-40GB    Off   | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

2) python checks
$ python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
2.2.0+cu117 11.7 True

-- mismatch: torch reports CUDA 11.7 support but system driver/runtime is 12.1. This can be OK (newer drivers backward compatible) but we've seen random "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" in other contexts when mixed libs exist.

3) nvcc --version inside container used for conversion
$ nvcc --version
Cuda compilation tools, release 11.7, V11.7.99

4) ldd on libtorch (conda env)
$ python -c "import torch, os; print(torch.__file__)"
.../site-packages/torch
$ ldd .../site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cudart
	libcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 (0x00007f...)

-- There are multiple libcudart versions on the image; ldconfig shows entries for libcudart.so.11 and libcudart.so.12. The conda torch build is binding to an 11.x ABI but the host has 12.x runtime symlinked in some locations.

5) Docker run check
$ docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime-ubuntu20.04 nvidia-smi\(ok)
$ docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi\(ok)

6) Repro command that produced OOM + driver error:
$ python serve.py --model ./7b-fp16 --batch-size 8\Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 214, in <module>
    runner = ModelRunner(args)
  File "serve.py", line 98, in __init__
    self.device = torch.device('cuda')
RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid device function
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

Then later/OOM: "CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.12 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 31.25 GiB already allocated; 1.00 GiB free; 32.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"

Hypotheses so far:
- Mixed libcudart.so versions on PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH (system and container) causing torch to dynamically bind to wrong CUDA runtime at load time.
- PyTorch wheel installed supports CUDA 11.7; driver >= 11.7 should be fine, but if any library (e.g., custom C++ ops, triton, onnxruntime, or libtorch from a different wheel) pulls in a different version ABI it can cause conflicts.
- There are multiple cuda-toolkit packages installed on host (/usr/local/cuda-11.0, /usr/local/cuda-11.7, /usr/local/cuda-12.1) and PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering differs between systemd service, docker runtime, and interactive shells.
- OOMs caused by a memory leak in our conversion step (we do not free CUDA memory between iterations) compounded by fragmentation; fallback after driver error shows inconsistent memory accounting.

What I tried (attempted mitigations):
- Force torch to use the cuda-only wheel matching host: pip install --force-reinstall "torch==2.2.0+cu121" -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html (note: internal policy means some envs still need cu117 build).
- Cleaned LD_LIBRARY_PATH and ensured /usr/local/cuda points to 11.7 during container run: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.7/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
- Added TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to reduce fragmentation: export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
- Used CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 to pin GPUs and run smaller batch sizes (batch 2/4 instead of 8) — reduced OOM frequency but not deterministic.
- Rebuilt custom ops with the system cuda (rebuild triton kernels, custom c++ ops).
- Tried running inside an official nvidia/cuda:11.7 container with matching nvcc and lib paths — that eliminated the driver mismatch errors but OOM still happened in heavy conversion.

Quick notes from logs and stacktraces:
- From /var/log/syslog around time of failure: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" — suggests GPU driver reset after severe failure.
- Python traceback sometimes shows: "Assertion `false && "Illegal memory access"' failed." from CUDA runtime.

Next steps / checklist (for me / infra):
- Reproduce inside a hermetic container with: nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime + conda env with torch+cu117. If clean, then mismatch is host contamination.
- Run ldconfig -p | grep libcudart to audit multiple installs. If multiple, remove unused symlinks or set container to point to specific library.
- Ask infra to pin driver to a validated version for our AMI family (either 535.x with 12.1 and use cu121 wheels, or install 520.x for 11.7 wheels).
- Add more telemetry: before model load print torch.cuda.memory_summary(), and catch OOM to dump allocation map (torch.cuda.memory_reserved/allocated).
- Add a preflight script to check "python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())'" in the startup and fail fast with a clear message linking to this doc.
- Try enabling "CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1" on a repro run to get a more deterministic backtrace for illegal access.

Notes for escalation email to infra (draft bullet points):
- Observed intermittent: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" while torch reports CUDA 11.7 ABI but nvidia-smi reports CUDA 12.1. There are multiple libcudart versions visible on the host.
- Repro steps included above; consistent elimination of mismatch when running in official 11.7 container, but still hitting OOMs in conversion workloads.
- Request: help standardize AMI to one driver/toolkit pairing (we suggest testing with driver 535 + cu121 wheels, or downgrade system driver to match widely used cu117 internal wheels).
- Request access to the AMI build logs and current ldconfig state for affected machines.

Random helpful links/refs I've used: 
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/12345 (example: "RuntimeError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version")
- https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/support-matrix/index.html
- Internal infra ticket: INFRA-1423 (GPU driver mismatch investigation)

Unresolved questions / TODOs for me:
- Confirm whether any Python packages in the env ship their own cuda runtime (.so files) — ldd every .so in site-packages that links to cudart.
- Check whether our model conversion step uses CUDA unified memory or calls cuMemAlloc directly.
- Run a small C++ cuda sample that prints runtime vs driver API versions to differentiate which component is complaining.

Short-term workaround for product tests: run conversion in a dedicated job on a pinned AMI/container combination that I verified (11.7 container + cu117 torch wheel) and lower batch sizes.

Longer-term: add an "inference runtime health" check to deployment pipelines that asserts CUDA/driver/torch ABI compatibility and rejects deployments that have mixed runtimes.

Personality notes: this is messy, often noisy — keep incremental notes here. If you copy/paste any outputs into tickets, redact instance ids.
